title: Frontend: Chinese Remainder Theorem
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Chinese Remainder Theorem. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({residues,moduli}) using decimal integer strings. Moduli are >1 and must be pairwise coprime. Return {value,modulus} decimal strings for the least nonnegative solution modulo their product. Empty system returns {value:0,modulus:1}. Noncoprime moduli throw Not coprime.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Let M be the product of moduli and Mi=M/mi.
alternativeApproaches: Implement generalized pairwise merging and return no solution when the residue difference is not divisible by the gcd.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Negative residue; modulus one policy; coprime system.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
